title: Il Trapassato Prossimo
subtitle: The past before the past — what had already happened.
objectives: Form the trapassato prossimo with the imperfetto of avere/essere + past participle
Use it to mark an action that happened before another past action
Apply the same auxiliary and agreement rules as the passato prossimo

content.intro: When you need to describe an event that had already finished before another past event, Italian reaches one step further back than the passato prossimo: the trapassato prossimo.
content.explanation: Formed exactly like the passato prossimo, but with the auxiliary in the imperfetto instead of the present: avevo parlato (I had spoken), ero partito (I had left). Every rule you already know — which verbs take essere, when the participle agrees — carries over unchanged.

rules.heading: a) Two past events, one earlier than the other
rules.body: The earlier event goes in the trapassato prossimo; the later one in the passato prossimo or imperfetto: Quando sono arrivato, il treno era già partito. (When I arrived, the train had already left.)

rules.heading: b) Common with già, non ancora, appena
rules.body: Non avevo mai visto un tramonto così. (I had never seen a sunset like that.) Aveva appena finito quando ho chiamato. (He had just finished when I called.)

examples.it: Quando sono arrivata, la lezione era già iniziata.
examples.en: When I arrived, the lesson had already started.

examples.it: Non avevo mai mangiato il sushi prima di quel viaggio.
examples.en: I had never eaten sushi before that trip.

examples.it: Avevamo già prenotato l'albergo quando hanno cancellato il volo.
examples.en: We had already booked the hotel when they cancelled the flight.

examples.it: Era già partito quando ho chiamato a casa sua.
examples.en: He had already left when I called his house.

commonMistakes.wrong: Quando sono arrivata, la lezione è già iniziata.
commonMistakes.right: Quando sono arrivata, la lezione era già iniziata.
commonMistakes.why: The starting of the lesson happened before the arrival, so it needs the trapassato prossimo, not the passato prossimo.
Andare takes essere, and this doesn't change in the trapassato prossimo — only the auxiliary's tense changes, not which auxiliary is used.

items.prompt: Quando sono tornato a casa, mia madre ___ (già - cucinare) la cena.
items.explanation: Trapassato prossimo for the earlier event.

items.prompt: Non ___ (io - mai vedere) un film così bello prima.
items.explanation: Trapassato prossimo of vedere: avevo visto.

items.prompt: "When I woke up, everyone had already left."
items.explanation: The leaving happened before the waking up — trapassato prossimo.

summary: Trapassato prossimo = imperfetto of avere/essere + past participle.
Marks an action completed before another past action or reference point.
Same auxiliary-choice and agreement rules as the passato prossimo — only the auxiliary's own tense changes.
